/-!
# Hadwiger conjecture (combinatorial geometry)

The Hadwiger conjecture (also called the Levi–Hadwiger conjecture or the Hadwiger–Levi covering
problem) states that every convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ can be covered by $2^n$ or fewer smaller
positively homothetic copies of itself, and that $2^n$ copies are needed if and only if the body
is a parallelepiped.

Here a convex body is a compact convex set with nonempty interior, as in the primary
literature. The Wikipedia article states the covering bound for all bounded convex sets; for
convex bodies this is equivalent to covering $K$ by $2^n$ translates of its interior.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Hadwiger conjecture (combinatorial geometry)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger_conjecture_%28combinatorial_geometry%29)
- [Ha57] Hadwiger, H., _Ungelöste Probleme Nr. 20_. Elemente der Mathematik 12 (1957), 121.
- [HSTV22] Huang, H., Slomka, B. A., Tkocz, T., Vritsiou, B.-H., _Improved bounds for Hadwiger's
  covering problem via thin-shell estimates_. J. Eur. Math. Soc. 24 (2022).
  [arXiv:1811.12548](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.12548)
- [CvHMT23] Campos, M., van Hintum, P., Morris, R., Tiba, M., _Towards Hadwiger's conjecture via
  Bourgain slicing_. Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN (2023).
  [arXiv:2206.11227](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.11227)
-/

blocks.docstring:
`CoveredBySmallerHomothets K m` says that `K ⊆ ℝⁿ` is covered by `m` smaller positively
homothetic copies of itself: there are scalars $s_1, \dots, s_m$ with $0 < s_i < 1$ and
translation vectors $v_1, \dots, v_m$ such that
$$K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{m} (s_i K + v_i).$$
Copies may coincide, so for nonempty `K` this also expresses coverability by at most `m` copies.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib has AffineMap.homothety and pointwise Set operations (Set.smulSet, Set.vaddSet) but no notion of covering by homothets; FormalConjecturesForMathlib and nearby files (ErdosProblems/769 has an axis-parallel cube-specific notion) have nothing reusable.
justification.name: HadwigerConjecture.CoveredBySmallerHomothets
justification.why_needed: Expresses 'K can be covered by m smaller (positive, ratio in (0,1)) homothetic copies of itself', needed both for the main statement and to form the set of admissible m in the equality case.

blocks.name: CoveredBySmallerHomothets
blocks.text:
/--
`CoveredBySmallerHomothets K m` says that `K ⊆ ℝⁿ` is covered by `m` smaller positively
homothetic copies of itself: there are scalars $s_1, \dots, s_m$ with $0 < s_i < 1$ and
translation vectors $v_1, \dots, v_m$ such that
$$K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{m} (s_i K + v_i).$$
Copies may coincide, so for nonempty `K` this also expresses coverability by at most `m` copies.
-/
def CoveredBySmallerHomothets {n : ℕ} (K : Set (ℝ^n)) (m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (s : Fin m → ℝ) (v : Fin m → ℝ^n),
    (∀ i, s i ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) ∧ K ⊆ ⋃ i, v i +ᵥ s i • K

blocks.code:
def IsParallelepiped {n : ℕ} (K : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ (ℝ^n)) (x : ℝ^n), K = x +ᵥ parallelepiped b
blocks.docstring:
`IsParallelepiped K` says that `K ⊆ ℝⁿ` is an $n$-dimensional parallelepiped: a translate of
the closed parallelepiped $\{\sum_i t_i b_i \mid 0 \le t_i \le 1\}$ spanned by a basis
$b_1, \dots, b_n$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$, that is, the image of the unit cube $[0,1]^n$ under an
affine bijection.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's `parallelepiped (v : ι → E)` and `Module.Basis.parallelepiped` give the parallelepiped spanned by a given family (anchored at 0); the definition is just the predicate 'K is a translate of one of these for some basis'. Arxiv/2607.03582 has a planar IsParallelogramAtOrigin which is not general enough.
justification.name: HadwigerConjecture.IsParallelepiped
justification.why_needed: Expresses 'K is an n-dimensional parallelepiped in ℝ^n' (translate of the parallelepiped spanned by a basis), needed for the equality case.

blocks.name: IsParallelepiped
blocks.text:
/--
`IsParallelepiped K` says that `K ⊆ ℝⁿ` is an $n$-dimensional parallelepiped: a translate of
the closed parallelepiped $\{\sum_i t_i b_i \mid 0 \le t_i \le 1\}$ spanned by a basis
$b_1, \dots, b_n$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$, that is, the image of the unit cube $[0,1]^n$ under an
affine bijection.
-/
def IsParallelepiped {n : ℕ} (K : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ (ℝ^n)) (x : ℝ^n), K = x +ᵥ parallelepiped b

@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isParallelepiped_unitCube (n : ℕ) :
    IsParallelepiped (parallelepiped (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ)) :=
  ⟨(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis, 0, by simp⟩
blocks.docstring: The unit cube $[0,1]^n$ is a parallelepiped.
blocks.name: isParallelepiped_unitCube
blocks.text:
/-- The unit cube $[0,1]^n$ is a parallelepiped. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isParallelepiped_unitCube (n : ℕ) :
    IsParallelepiped (parallelepiped (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ)) :=
  ⟨(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis, 0, by simp⟩

@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem coveredBySmallerHomothets_singleton {n : ℕ} (x : ℝ^n) :
    CoveredBySmallerHomothets {x} 1 :=
  ⟨fun _ => 1 / 2, fun _ => (1 / 2 : ℝ) • x, fun _ => by norm_num, by
    simp only [Set.smul_set_singleton, Set.vadd_set_singleton, Set.iUnion_const, vadd_eq_add,
      ← add_smul]
    norm_num⟩

**Hadwiger conjecture.** Every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with
nonempty interior) can be covered by at most $2^n$ smaller homothetic copies of itself: there are
$2^n$ scalars $s_i$ with $0 < s_i < 1$ and $2^n$ translation vectors $v_i$ such that

**Hadwiger conjecture.** Every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with
nonempty interior) can be covered by at most $2^n$ smaller homothetic copies of itself: there are
$2^n$ scalars $s_i$ with $0 < s_i < 1$ and $2^n$ translation vectors $v_i$ such that

theorem hadwiger_conjecture (n : ℕ) (K : Set (ℝ^n)) (hK : Convex ℝ K) (hKc : IsCompact K)

@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture.variants.equality_case (n : ℕ) (K : Set (ℝ^n)) (hK : Convex ℝ K)
    (hKc : IsCompact K) (hKi : (interior K).Nonempty) :
    IsLeast {m | CoveredBySmallerHomothets K m} (2 ^ n) ↔ IsParallelepiped K := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Hadwiger conjecture, equality case.** For a convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact
convex set with nonempty interior), the upper bound $2^n$ is necessary if and only if $K$ is a
parallelepiped: the least number of smaller homothetic copies of $K$ needed to cover $K$ equals
$2^n$ exactly when $K$ is a parallelepiped.

The nonempty interior hypothesis excludes lower-dimensional bodies, for which fewer copies
suffice and "parallelepiped" would not mean an $n$-dimensional affine image of the cube.

claims.decomposer_note: The Prop is: for every n and every bounded convex (convex body: compact, nonempty interior in the papers' convention) K ⊆ ℝ^n there exist scalars 0 < s_i < 1 and translation vectors v_i, i = 1..2^n, with K ⊆ ⋃ (s_i • K + v_i); the '2n' in the list entry is 2^n (exponent lost in plain text), 'smaller copies' means positively homothetic copies with ratio strictly less than 1 (equivalently, for bodies with nonempty interior, 2^n translates of the interior of K), and the illumination formulation by floodlights is an equivalent restatement of this same question rather than a distinct one; degenerate/lower-dimensional or empty K are harmless for the ≤ 2^n bound but the formalizer should decide whether to assume nonempty interior as the papers do.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same core Prop (∃ 2^n ratios in (0,1) and translations with K ⊆ ⋃ (v_i +ᵥ s_i • K); c01 uses an equivalent pointwise-membership form). Verified the pointwise semantics: y ∈ v +ᵥ s • K ↔ ∃ x ∈ K, v + s•x = y. Candidates split on the domain: c02/c04/c05 use the article's 'bounded convex' formulation, c01/c03/c06/c07/c08 the primary-literature 'convex body' (compact, convex, nonempty interior). Both are faithful and equivalent given ∀ n (a lower-dimensional/non-closed bounded convex set is covered by 2^m ≤ 2^n smaller homothets of itself once the convex-body case holds in its dimension m; a homothet of cl K is contained in a slightly larger homothet of K). The list entry literally says 'n-dimensional convex bodies', so the convex-body version was shipped. Exactly-2^n indices encode 'at most 2^n' since copies may coincide and K is nonempty. c07 chosen for clean bespoke definitions, API tests, and the collection's ℝ^n notation; edits: explicit binders instead of a shadowed `variable`, tidied docstrings, dropped unverifiable page numbers from references.
claims.source_text: covering n-dimensional convex bodies with at most 2n smaller copies
claims.text_span: covering n-dimensional convex bodies with at most 2n smaller copies

claims.decomposer_note: Stronger subordinate form stated by the article as part of the conjecture: for every convex body K ⊆ ℝ^n (nonempty interior needed here so that 'parallelepiped' means an n-dimensional affine image of the cube), the minimal number of smaller homothetic copies needed to cover K equals 2^n iff K is a parallelepiped; the 'if' direction (parallelepipeds need 2^n copies, 2^n copies scaled by 1/2 suffice) is known, the 'only if' direction (every non-parallelepiped body needs fewer than 2^n copies) is the open part, and both fit in one biconditional Prop.
claims.reviewer_why: Stated as IsLeast {m | CoveredBySmallerHomothets K m} (2^n) ↔ IsParallelepiped K for convex bodies K, where IsParallelepiped K means K = x +ᵥ parallelepiped b for a basis b of ℝ^n (n-dimensional affine image of the closed unit cube). IsLeast avoids junk values (c04's ℕ-valued sInf and c05's ℕ∞ infimum are equivalent on-domain but less direct; c01 spells IsLeast out by hand; c06's affine-equivalence-image definition of parallelepiped is equivalent). Both directions live in one biconditional: 'if' (parallelepipeds need exactly 2^n copies: each smaller positive homothet contains at most one vertex; 2^n half-scaled copies suffice) is correct under these definitions, 'only if' is the open part. Boundary cases checked: n = 0 (K = {0}, needs exactly 1 = 2^0 copy, is a parallelepiped) and n = 1 (convex bodies are nondegenerate closed segments, need exactly 2 copies, all are parallelepipeds) are consistent.
claims.source_text: the upper bound of 2n is necessary if and only if the body is a parallelepiped
claims.text_span: the upper bound of 2n is necessary if and only if the body is a parallelepiped

context:
In combinatorial geometry, the Hadwiger conjecture states that any convex body in n-dimensional Euclidean space can be covered by 2n or fewer smaller bodies homothetic with the original body, and that furthermore, the upper bound of 2n is necessary if and only if the body is a parallelepiped. There also exists an equivalent formulation in terms of the number of floodlights needed to illuminate the body.
The Hadwiger conjecture is named after Hugo Hadwiger, who included it on a list of unsolved problems in 1957; it was, however, previously studied by Levi (1955) and independently, Gohberg & Markus (1960). Additionally, there is a different Hadwiger conjecture concerning graph coloring, and in some sources the geometric Hadwiger conjecture is also called the Levi–Hadwiger conjecture or the Hadwiger–Levi covering problem.
The conjecture remains unsolved even in three dimensions, though the two-dimensional case was resolved by Levi (1955).

decomposition_objections.text: None. The table's reading (2n = 2^n; smaller copies = positive homothets with ratio in (0,1); convex body with nonempty interior; equality case as 'minimal number = 2^n iff parallelepiped') is consistent with the Wikipedia article and the cited papers.

/-!
# Hadwiger conjecture (combinatorial geometry)

The Hadwiger conjecture (also called the Levi–Hadwiger conjecture or the Hadwiger–Levi covering
problem) states that every convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ can be covered by $2^n$ or fewer smaller
positively homothetic copies of itself, and that $2^n$ copies are needed if and only if the body
is a parallelepiped.

Here a convex body is a compact convex set with nonempty interior, as in the primary
literature. The Wikipedia article states the covering bound for all bounded convex sets; for
convex bodies this is equivalent to covering $K$ by $2^n$ translates of its interior.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Hadwiger conjecture (combinatorial geometry)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hadwiger_conjecture_%28combinatorial_geometry%29)
- [Ha57] Hadwiger, H., _Ungelöste Probleme Nr. 20_. Elemente der Mathematik 12 (1957), 121.
- [HSTV22] Huang, H., Slomka, B. A., Tkocz, T., Vritsiou, B.-H., _Improved bounds for Hadwiger's
  covering problem via thin-shell estimates_. J. Eur. Math. Soc. 24 (2022).
  [arXiv:1811.12548](https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.12548)
- [CvHMT23] Campos, M., van Hintum, P., Morris, R., Tiba, M., _Towards Hadwiger's conjecture via
  Bourgain slicing_. Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN (2023).
  [arXiv:2206.11227](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.11227)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry Pointwise

namespace HadwigerConjecture

/--
`CoveredBySmallerHomothets K m` says that `K ⊆ ℝⁿ` is covered by `m` smaller positively
homothetic copies of itself: there are scalars $s_1, \dots, s_m$ with $0 < s_i < 1$ and
translation vectors $v_1, \dots, v_m$ such that
$$K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{m} (s_i K + v_i).$$
Copies may coincide, so for nonempty `K` this also expresses coverability by at most `m` copies.
-/
def CoveredBySmallerHomothets {n : ℕ} (K : Set (ℝ^n)) (m : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (s : Fin m → ℝ) (v : Fin m → ℝ^n),
    (∀ i, s i ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1) ∧ K ⊆ ⋃ i, v i +ᵥ s i • K

/--
`IsParallelepiped K` says that `K ⊆ ℝⁿ` is an $n$-dimensional parallelepiped: a translate of
the closed parallelepiped $\{\sum_i t_i b_i \mid 0 \le t_i \le 1\}$ spanned by a basis
$b_1, \dots, b_n$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$, that is, the image of the unit cube $[0,1]^n$ under an
affine bijection.
-/
def IsParallelepiped {n : ℕ} (K : Set (ℝ^n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ (ℝ^n)) (x : ℝ^n), K = x +ᵥ parallelepiped b

/-- The unit cube $[0,1]^n$ is a parallelepiped. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem isParallelepiped_unitCube (n : ℕ) :
    IsParallelepiped (parallelepiped (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ)) :=
  ⟨(EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ).toBasis, 0, by simp⟩

/-- A single point is covered by one smaller homothetic copy of itself. -/
@[category test, AMS 52]
theorem coveredBySmallerHomothets_singleton {n : ℕ} (x : ℝ^n) :
    CoveredBySmallerHomothets {x} 1 :=
  ⟨fun _ => 1 / 2, fun _ => (1 / 2 : ℝ) • x, fun _ => by norm_num, by
    simp only [Set.smul_set_singleton, Set.vadd_set_singleton, Set.iUnion_const, vadd_eq_add,
      ← add_smul]
    norm_num⟩

/--
**Hadwiger conjecture.** Every convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact convex set with
nonempty interior) can be covered by at most $2^n$ smaller homothetic copies of itself: there are
$2^n$ scalars $s_i$ with $0 < s_i < 1$ and $2^n$ translation vectors $v_i$ such that
$$K \subseteq \bigcup_{i=1}^{2^n} (s_i K + v_i).$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture (n : ℕ) (K : Set (ℝ^n)) (hK : Convex ℝ K) (hKc : IsCompact K)
    (hKi : (interior K).Nonempty) :
    CoveredBySmallerHomothets K (2 ^ n) := by
  sorry

/--
**Hadwiger conjecture, equality case.** For a convex body $K \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ (a compact
convex set with nonempty interior), the upper bound $2^n$ is necessary if and only if $K$ is a
parallelepiped: the least number of smaller homothetic copies of $K$ needed to cover $K$ equals
$2^n$ exactly when $K$ is a parallelepiped.

The nonempty interior hypothesis excludes lower-dimensional bodies, for which fewer copies
suffice and "parallelepiped" would not mean an $n$-dimensional affine image of the cube.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem hadwiger_conjecture.variants.equality_case (n : ℕ) (K : Set (ℝ^n)) (hK : Convex ℝ K)
    (hKc : IsCompact K) (hKi : (interior K).Nonempty) :
    IsLeast {m | CoveredBySmallerHomothets K m} (2 ^ n) ↔ IsParallelepiped K := by
  sorry

end HadwigerConjecture

items: Ambient space is EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) (repo's scoped notation ℝ^n); the problem is affine-invariant so the choice of norm is immaterial.

Convex body = Convex ℝ K ∧ IsCompact K ∧ (interior K).Nonempty (the papers' convention and the list entry's 'n-dimensional convex bodies'). Wikipedia's 'Formal statement' section quantifies over all bounded convex sets instead; I chose the convex-body hypotheses as the table notes suggest, and because nonempty interior is needed for the equality case anyway. Both slots are therefore stated for the same class of sets. This makes slot 1 formally weaker than the 'bounded convex set' reading (degenerate/non-closed bounded convex sets are not covered by the statement), though the two readings are standardly regarded as the same conjecture.

'Smaller homothetic copies' = positive homothets with ratio s_i ∈ Ioo 0 1 and arbitrary translation v_i, written v i +ᵥ s i • K = {s_i x + v_i | x ∈ K}, exactly Wikipedia's s_i K + v_i with 0 < s_i < 1. Negative ratios are excluded, as in the source.
'At most 2^n copies' is encoded as exactly 2^n indexed copies (Fin (2^n)) that may coincide, matching Wikipedia's formula; for nonempty K this is equivalent to covering by ≤ 2^n copies.

Equality case: 'the minimal number of copies equals 2^n' is encoded as IsLeast {m | CoveredBySmallerHomothets K m} (2^n) (2^n copies suffice and no fewer do), following the table's notes. This avoids an sInf-based covering number (sInf ∅ = 0 junk value). An alternative reading of 'the bound 2^n is necessary' as merely 2^n ∈ lowerBounds {m | ...} coincides with IsLeast under the first slot.

Parallelepiped = n-dimensional parallelepiped: ∃ basis b of ℝ^n (Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ (ℝ^n)) and x with K = x +ᵥ parallelepiped b, using Mathlib's `parallelepiped`. Lower-dimensional parallelepipeds are excluded, which is harmless since K has nonempty interior. Boundary cases checked: n = 0 (K = {0} is a parallelepiped and needs exactly 1 = 2^0 copy) and n = 1 (every convex body is a segment, hence a parallelepiped needing 2 copies) are consistent with the biconditional.
The known refinement 'in which case all scalars may be chosen to be 1/2' and the illumination formulation are not separate slots and are not stated.
Two small `category test` lemmas exercise the bespoke definitions (unit cube is a parallelepiped; a singleton is covered by one smaller copy).

reviewer_notes: The plain-text '2n' in the list entry is 2^n (exponent lost), as the article's displayed formula and all candidates agree. No candidate omitted a slot; all compiled. Extra non-slot declarations in c02/c04 (Levi's planar case, textbook parallelepiped lemmas) were not shipped since only the adjudicated slots plus small `category test` lemmas for the bespoke definitions belong in the final file. The choice between 'bounded convex' and 'convex body (compact, nonempty interior)' for slot 1 is a genuine ambiguity in the sources (article's formal statement vs. list entry/papers); both are equivalent as conjectures and the convex-body reading was chosen to match the list-entry text and to share hypotheses with the equality case. Final file compiles under `lake env lean` with only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings.

title: Hadwiger conjecture (combinatorial geometry)
